_comment: Gemini/OpenAI/Claude-compatible function-declaration schemas for the preference-setting tools described in PREFERENCE_API.md (repo root). This file is the paste-ready artifact -- copy the `tools` array directly into a model call's tool-declaration list. Standard JSON Schema throughout (lowercase types), so this is portable across providers, not Gemini-specific. Keep this file and PREFERENCE_API.md in sync by hand until there's a codegen step; PREFERENCE_API.md's worked examples reference these exact parameter names.

tools.name: set_preferred_work_hours
tools.description: Set the single daily time window the student prefers to do flexible schoolwork in. Call this when they state a general daily rhythm, e.g. 'I like working in the evenings', 'mornings are my best time', 'I don't want to study before noon'. This REPLACES any previously set preferred hours -- there is only ever one active window, not a list.

end_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM, e.g. '23:00' for 11pm. Must be later than start_time.

strength.description: How strongly to favor this window over other times. 'moderate' is the tested default and correct unless the student explicitly emphasizes how important this is ('I REALLY only want to work at night').

tools.name: set_daily_workload_limit
tools.description: Cap how many minutes of flexible schoolwork land on a given day (or every day). Call this when the student talks about feeling overloaded on certain days, wanting lighter days, or wanting a real rest day, e.g. 'Sundays should be light', 'don't pack more than a few hours a day', 'I'm burning out'. Can be called multiple times for DIFFERENT day-sets (e.g. once for weekdays generally, once for a stricter Sunday cap) -- those coexist. Calling it again for the SAME day-set replaces the previous limit for that day-set.

minutes_per_day.description: Max flexible-work minutes on an affected day. 240 (4 hours) is a reasonable general default; 60-120 for an explicit light/rest day.

days.description: Which days this cap applies to. OMIT ENTIRELY to apply to every day -- do not pass all seven days explicitly, that is a different (and slower) case than the general default.

strength.description: How hard the solver should try to respect this cap when the schedule is tight. 'firm' is right for an explicit rest day; 'moderate' for a general daily cap.

tools.name: protect_time_block
tools.description: Make a recurring block of time completely off-limits to flexible schoolwork -- total protection, not a soft preference. Call this for social time, sports, religious observance, or any other 'never schedule anything here' request, e.g. 'don't touch my Friday nights', 'I have church Sunday mornings', 'keep game nights free'. Can be called multiple times for DIFFERENT blocks -- they all stay protected simultaneously. Calling it again for the exact same days+window updates that one block (e.g. to widen it).

days.description: Which days this protected block applies to.

start_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM start of the protected window.

end_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM end of the protected window. Use '24:00' for midnight, not '00:00'.

tools.name: set_break_habits
tools.description: Control how the solver values giving the student real breaks during a work stretch. Call this when they talk about needing breaks, burning out, or working too long without stopping, e.g. 'I need a real break every couple hours', 'don't let me grind for 4 hours straight', 'shorter breaks are fine, just don't work me to death'. This is a SOFT goal (minimize the worst unbroken stretch), not an absolute cutoff -- a genuinely urgent deadline can still occasionally produce a longer stretch than usual. Replaces any previous call -- only one active setting.

break_minutes.description: How long a gap has to be before it counts as a real break (shorter gaps don't reset the 'been working too long' counter). 45 is the tested default.

strength.description: How hard the solver should push to keep work stretches short. 'moderate' is the tested, recommended default. 'firm' measurably trades off against getting urgent work done early -- only use it if the student explicitly prioritizes breaks over finishing things ahead of schedule.

tools.name: set_task_spacing
tools.description: Control how strongly the solver avoids putting multiple sessions of the SAME assignment on the same day. Call this when the student talks about wanting to spread a big assignment out instead of cramming all its sessions together, or the opposite -- wanting to knock a task out in one day, e.g. 'spread my project work out more', 'don't put three problem-set sessions on the same day', 'I'd rather just power through an assignment in one sitting once I start'. There is always exactly one active setting for this -- calling it again replaces the previous one, it does not stack.

strength.description: How strongly to penalize same-day, same-task sessions. 'moderate' is the tested default (this schedule's setting before it was ever chat-adjustable) and correct unless the student is explicit about how important this is.

tools.name: set_urgency_emphasis
tools.description: Control how strongly the solver favors placing soon-due work earlier rather than later in the window. Call this when the student talks about wanting urgent deadlines handled sooner, or the opposite -- not wanting the schedule to always front-load whatever is due next, e.g. 'get urgent stuff done as early as possible', 'stop always rushing me toward the next deadline', 'I don't mind cutting it closer sometimes'. There is always exactly one active setting -- calling it again replaces the previous one.

strength.description: How strongly to reward earlier placement of urgent work. 'moderate' is the tested default (this schedule's setting before it was ever chat-adjustable) and correct unless the student is explicit about how important this is.

tools.name: set_minimum_gap
tools.description: Set the minimum real-world gap required between any two flexible study sessions -- a HARD rule, not a soft preference; the solver will never schedule two sessions closer together than this. Call this when the student explicitly asks for more (or less) buffer between back-to-back study blocks, e.g. 'give me at least half an hour between study sessions', 'I don't need much of a gap, 5 minutes is fine'. This is a DIFFERENT setting from set_break_habits (which is about how long a single unbroken work STRETCH can run before it counts as needing a break) -- this one is about the gap between two already-separate sessions.

minutes.description: Minimum minutes required between the end of one flexible session and the start of the next. 15 is the tested default (this schedule's setting before it was ever chat-adjustable).

tools.name: set_meal_window
tools.description: Set the time range a meal is allowed to happen within -- NOT an exact time. The solver places the meal freely anywhere inside this window, at whatever length works best around the rest of the schedule; it does not pin the meal to one fixed clock time. Call this when the student wants to change when they eat, e.g. 'I want breakfast earlier, like 6 to 8', 'lunch should be between 11 and 1:30', 'push dinner later, after 7'. Calling it again for the SAME meal replaces that meal's window -- each meal (breakfast/lunch/dinner) has exactly one active window at a time, independent of the other two.

meal.description: Which meal this window applies to.

start_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM, earliest the meal can start.

end_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM, latest the meal can end. Must leave enough room for duration_minutes -- e.g. a 45-minute meal needs at least 45 minutes between start_time and end_time.

duration_minutes.description: How long the meal itself takes. 45 is the tested default (this schedule's setting before it was ever chat-adjustable).

tools.name: set_commitment
tools.description: Add or update a personal commitment that needs real time on the calendar but isn't schoolwork -- gym, club meetings, a standing appointment, anything recurring. Two modes: 'locked' pins it to an EXACT time, like a class (use this when the student gives one specific time, e.g. 'club meets Wednesday 7 to 9pm, lock that in'). 'windowed' gives it a bounded RANGE the solver places freely within, wherever fits best each day -- possibly a different exact time day to day (use this when the student gives a range or says 'sometime around', e.g. 'I want to go to the gym every day sometime between 6 and 9am'). Calling this again for the SAME name replaces it -- this is also how you lock or unlock an existing commitment: just call it again with a different mode. There is no separate lock/unlock tool.

name.description: A short label for this commitment, e.g. 'Gym', 'Club Meeting'. Re-using the same name (case-insensitive) replaces the existing commitment by that name.

mode.description: 'locked' = exact, immovable time (like a class). 'windowed' = a range the solver places freely within.

days.description: Which days this recurs on. OMIT ENTIRELY for every day -- do not pass all seven explicitly.

start_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM. For 'locked', the exact start. For 'windowed', the earliest allowed start.

end_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM. For 'locked', the exact end. For 'windowed', the latest allowed end -- must leave enough room for duration_minutes.

duration_minutes.description: REQUIRED when mode is 'windowed' -- how long the commitment itself takes, within the window. Not used for 'locked' (start_time/end_time already give the exact span).

tools.name: add_task
tools.description: Add a new assignment/task for the solver to schedule study sessions for. Call this whenever the student describes a real piece of upcoming work that isn't already on their calendar -- a problem set, an essay, exam prep, a reading -- with at least a course and a deadline. This does NOT set any preference and does NOT choose when the work happens; it only describes the task. The solver (CP-SAT) still decides every session's actual time, exactly like it does for every other task. By default the task is split into sessions automatically (never more than about an hour each). Use session_plan ONLY when the student is explicit about the structure they want (an exact count and/or length of sessions) -- e.g. 'I want to do this in two 2-hour sessions and a short review', 'give me three 45-minute sessions for this', 'I'll do it in one sitting'. Don't invent a session_plan when the student just states a duration and deadline with no structure preference -- let the default split handle that.

title.description: A short, real name for the assignment, e.g. 'Problem Set 4' or 'Research Paper Draft'. Not an instruction -- just what it's called.

course_id.description: The exact course _id from the courses list already provided in context. Never invent or guess an id -- if the student's class isn't in that list, say so instead of calling this tool.

due_date.description: The real calendar date this is due, as YYYY-MM-DD. Resolve relative language ('due Friday', 'in 5 days', 'next week') against the current date already provided in context -- never guess a year or leave this vague.

due_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM the assignment is due. Defaults to 23:59 (a generic homework-portal deadline) if the student doesn't say -- omit rather than guess a specific time they never stated.

est_duration_min.description: Total estimated work time in minutes, e.g. 90 for 'an hour and a half', 300 for 'about 5 hours'. REQUIRED unless session_plan is given (in which case it's derived automatically as the sum -- omit this field entirely rather than compute the sum yourself).

splittable.description: Whether this can be split across multiple sessions at all. Set false only for something that must happen in one sitting (e.g. a timed practice exam) -- most schoolwork is splittable.

session_plan.description: OPTIONAL. An explicit, ordered list of session lengths in minutes when the student wants specific structure instead of the default automatic split -- e.g. [120, 120, 30] for 'two 2-hour sessions then a 30-minute review'. Each entry can be up to 4 hours (deliberately larger than the ~1-hour default cap, since asking for this is exactly how a student requests a longer deep-work block). Leave this out entirely for a normal 'just schedule it' request.

tools.name: remove_task
tools.description: Delete an assignment entirely -- not just a preference about it, the task itself and every session it would have produced. Call this when the student says something like 'actually cancel that assignment I added', 'delete the research paper task', 'that got extended to next month, remove it and I'll re-add it later', or 'the professor cancelled that assignment'. Works for any task visible in the current tasks list already provided in context, not only ones added earlier in this conversation. Always confirm which task in plain language if there's any doubt which one they mean -- deleting the wrong assignment is not reversible from chat.

task_id.description: The exact task _id to remove, from this conversation's own add_task result or from the current tasks list in context. Never guess an id.

tools.name: remove_preference
tools.description: Retract a previously set preference. Call this when the student says something like 'never mind that', 'actually forget the Sunday thing', 'I changed my mind about evenings', or any other request to undo or cancel a specific earlier preference. Always confirm which preference in plain language before or after calling this if there's any doubt which one they mean.

preference_type.description: Which kind of preference to remove.

match.description: Needed for daily_workload_limit or protected_time_block when MORE THAN ONE is currently active, for meal_window whenever more than one meal's window is active (which is normal -- breakfast/lunch/dinner each have their own), and for commitment whenever more than one commitment is active (also normal -- gym and club meetings coexist) -- repeat enough of the original call's parameters to identify which one (e.g. {"days": ["Fri", "Sat"]} for a protected block, {"meal": "lunch"} for a meal window, or {"name": "Gym"} for a commitment). Omit for preferred_work_hours/break_habits (there's only ever one), or when only one entry of the given type currently exists.

tools.name: list_current_preferences
tools.description: Read back every preference currently active for this student. Call this before a remove_preference if you're not sure exactly what's set, or whenever the student asks what's currently affecting their schedule ('what have I told you so far?', 'what's my current setup?').
